issues.description: The problem statement instructs that the SealSaloon's stock should be initialized in the constructor as a final per-instance field, but elsewhere explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static/shared across all instances. This is a contradictory requirement about the nature and initialization of the 'stock' attribute and will confuse students whether to implement stock as an instance final field (initialized in the constructor) or as a static (shared) field.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the requirement consistent. Either: (A) Require a static final shared stock (preferred given later notes) and update the wording that only 'orders' should be initialized in the no-arg constructor while 'stock' is declared and initialized as 'private static final Stock stock = new Stock();' (or in a static initializer). Or: (B) if the intent is per-instance stock, remove the note that 'stock' must be static. Update the problem statement to explicitly state where and how to initialize each attribute to avoid ambiguity.

issues.description: The UML and textual description show acceptSupplyDelivery as a public method (+acceptSupplyDelivery), but the reference implementation declares it as package-private (no access modifier). This visibility difference may confuse students about the required API visibility and could cause test-access issues if callers expect a public method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent with the UML/specification by declaring the method public static in the implementation and in examples (i.e., 'public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(...)'). Update the solution and any guidance in the problem statement to explicitly require a public static method.
